title: Hours of Work and Rest Law, 5711-1951
source_id: ס"ח תשי"א, 204 (Sefer HaChukim 5711, p 204); Knesset IsraelLawID 2000019; Wikisource page 'חוק שעות עבודה ומנוחה'
verified_how: Knesset Open Data KNS_IsraelLaw record fetched 23 September 2026: IsraelLawID 2000019, Name 'חוק שעות עבודה ומנוחה, התשי"א-1951', KnessetNum 1, PublicationDate 1951-05-22, ValidityStartDate 1951-09-27, LatestPublicationDate 2018-06-21, LawValidityDesc 'תקף', ValidityFinishDate null, LastUpdatedDate 2025-09-15. KNS_LawBinding returned 19 rows: 1 'החוק המקורי' with PageNumber '204' and 18 'מתקן' rows. The Hebrew Wikisource page prints 'חוק שעות עבודה ומנוחה, תשי"א–1951', citation 'ס"ח תשי"א, 204' with amending years 5724 through 5778, and no repeal marker. A first read of the Wikisource page appeared to show a 5785/2025 change; a targeted re-read established that the two 5785-2025 items are general overtime permits issued UNDER the Law and published as notices - 'הודעה על מתן היתר כללי להעסקת עובדים בשעות נוספות (הוראת שעה), התשפ"ה–2025' and 'הודעה על מתן היתר כללי בדבר שעות נוספות והפסקות בתחבורה (הוראת שעה), התשפ"ה–2025' - not amendments to the statute. The official LatestPublicationDate of 2018-06-21 is therefore correct for statutory amendments, and there is no discrepancy between the two sources.
notes: TOPIC ALLOCATION (asked for explicitly): filed under Payroll/wages, not Leave/holiday pay. Reason: the Law's operative money rules are payroll computation rules - it caps the ordinary working day and week and then fixes the PREMIUM RATES payable for overtime and for work on the weekly rest, so in practice it is the statute that determines what a lawful payslip must pay for hours worked. Its weekly-rest and rest-break provisions are about mandatory non-working hours within a working week, which is a different thing from paid annual or holiday leave; Israel puts paid leave entitlement in the Annual Leave Law and the Sick Pay Law, which are filed under Leave/holiday pay. A human who prefers a 'working time' topic should note this Act would be its natural anchor. Also note that a large part of the practical regime sits in general permits (היתר כללי) issued under the Law rather than in the Law itself - see verified_how - so an encoding of the statute alone will not reproduce the sectoral overtime rules.
